🚀 CCTV_YOLO | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Real-time object detection on live video streams, optimized for speed and high-resolution output, suitable for surveillance applications.
✨ Key Features: • YOLOv5n6 Model • Low-resolution Processing for High-speed Inference • High-resolution Output with Detections Drawn • Gradio Interface for Real-time Interaction
📖 Summary: This repository implements a fast, real-time object detection system for CCTV surveillance using the YOLOv5n6 model. It achieves high processing speeds by performing inference on low-resolution frames and then drawing the detection results onto high-resolution video streams, all accessible through an interactive Gradio interface.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 PriceGhost | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a reliable, self-hosted solution for tracking product prices across the web, ensuring accuracy through a unique price verification system and offering customizable notifications.
✨ Key Features: • Self-hosted price tracking • Monitors product prices from any website
📖 Summary: PriceGhost is a self-hosted price tracking application designed to monitor product prices from any website. It employs a unique multi-strategy extraction system, including JSON-LD, site-specific scrapers, generic CSS, and AI analysis, to accurately determine product prices. Users are presented with a Price Voting Modal to confirm the correct price, ensuring accurate tracking and preventing common price tracking errors.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ LemonSees | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide security analysts with a unified, agentless platform for monitoring, investigating, and responding to security incidents across their infrastructure using only SSH connections.
✨ Key Features: • Agentless monitoring via SSH • Comprehensive SOC domains (SIEM/XDR, EDR, NDR, CTI, SOAR, GRC)
📖 Summary: LemonSees is an agentless Security Operations Center (SOC) and Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform designed for L1/L2/L3 analysts. It leverages SSH connections as the sole means of interaction, eliminating the need for any server-side installations, and provides a comprehensive suite of tools for monitoring, threat intelligence, and incident response directly from a Windows desktop application.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 Mekka | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a compact, experimental backend for developers and AI agents working together on applications, facilitating rapid local development and self-hosted deployments with integrated tools like a Studio.
✨ Key Features: • Experimental source-available backend • SQLite and libSQL support • Typed data API • Local authentication • Object Storage
📖 Summary: Mekka is an experimental, source-available backend for SQLite and libSQL, designed for human-and-agent-native workflows. It offers a typed data API, local authentication, object storage, and realtime primitives, with a focus on fast local iteration and self-hosted deployments.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 rubick | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide developers and operators with a transparent and reliable desktop interface for interacting with and monitoring Kubernetes clusters, especially in identifying and diagnosing issues.
✨ Key Features: • Honest status reporting (shows failures, not just fields) • Detailed path analysis (Ingress -> Service -> pods)
📖 Summary: Rubick is a cross-platform desktop client for Kubernetes that aims to provide a more honest and transparent view of cluster status. It differentiates itself by clearly indicating failures and providing detailed explanations for why certain resources might not be functioning as expected, unlike other tools that might present a misleadingly healthy status.
